messages:
robin (pm): Quick design review — the eval-run toolbar in compact density feels noisy and confusing. Posting a few concrete nits and a proposed copy/layout change.

matt (design): +1. Main problems I see: primary approve CTA sits right next to the overflow menu, icons are ambiguous (checkmark vs circle), and focus order in keyboard nav feels off. Figma mock here: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/eval-toolbar

jin (eng): From eng perspective: compact mode currently reuses full-mode DOM order. Moving approve left will require DOM reorder which affects keyboard traversal and our e2e selectors. Not impossible but heads-up on test churn.

aria (a11y): A11y nits: approve button needs an explicit aria-label (e.g., "Approve run") and we should use aria-pressed for toggle states. Also the green badge used for the CTA is ~3.2:1 on contrast — we need 4.5:1 for small text.

elaine (prod): Copy question: do we want the CTA to read "Approve" or "Approve run"? For audit logs it helps to include the noun. Consistency with other modals is important.

matt (design): My proposed microcopy: primary CTA = "Approve run" (short + explicit), secondary = "Request changes"; overflow tooltip = "More actions". I also propose moving the CTA one position left so it doesn't sit next to kebab.

sam (research): :thinking_face: Also consider keyboard shortcut for fast reviewers. 'k' is common for list nav though. Could show accelerator in tooltip.

jin (eng): We use 'k' for list jumps already, so conflict. Maybe Shift+A or Ctrl+Enter for approve-from-row. We can surface it in a hover affordance. Implementation overhead small.

aria (a11y): Screenreader note: when opening the overflow menu focus must move into the menu and be trapped; announce number of actions with aria-live politely (e.g., "3 actions available"). Also ensure menu items have clear text, not just icons.

robin (pm): Bulk-approve modal copy is another item — current copy "Approve X runs" is terse. Suggest: "Approve X runs — this will mark them as approved. You can revert approvals from the rollouts tab." Keep the primary action verb-focused.

matt (design): Layout mock: swap icon order so approve CTA is leftmost in compact rows, then segue into details and overflow. I'll add spacing and reduce density of the score badge.

jin (eng): Estimating effort: DOM reorder + e2e updates = 2-3 dev days, a11y fixes + aria labels = 1 day, copy/microcopy tweaks = quick.

eva (ux-bot): ux-annotation-bot: Attached design comments and redlines: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/annotations — tagged matt, aria.

aria (a11y): One more color token suggestion: switch from green-500 to green-600 and add a focused outline (3px solid token) for keyboard focus. That should hit contrast and visibility.

robin (pm): Decision proposal: do layout reorder in canary channel, adopt copy "Approve run", implement aria-labels and contrast change. Jin please file PR; matt to upload new screenshots; aria to validate in the canary build.

jin (eng): Filing PR now — branch feature/eval-toolbar-reorder, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pulse/pull/4123 (draft). Will include changelog and e2e updates.

matt (design): Uploaded 3 updated screenshots to the figma page and added hover state for accelerator.

elaine (prod): I'll update the product spec and rollout notes (canary -> stable). Also logging: ensure audit entry includes run id + actor for bulk-approve.

aria (a11y): I'll run axe + NVDA on the canary once PR is up. Quick checklist: aria-labels, menu focus trap, color tokens, visible focus ring.

robin (pm): Great — thanks everyone. If no major blockers from a11y or infra in 48h we'll ship to canary. :rocket:

matt (design): small follow-up: tooltip for the approve icon should include the shortcut (e.g., "Approve run — Shift+A").

jin (eng): noted, will add data-shortcut attr to the button for tooltip rendering.

elaine (prod): Thanks team. I'll post a short release note and a screenshot in #release-war-room when canary is deployed.

robin (pm): End of thread — tagging for follow-ups: @aria (a11y), @jin (eng), @matt (design).
